svg.title: Tower Ownership Go/No-Go Gates
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-05-tower-ownership-go-no-go; chapter number: 5; title: Tower Ownership Go/No-Go Gates; subtitle: The first tenant pays the bills; every tenant after that pays the owner; caption: One tenant can yield as little as 1% to 3% with paybacks of 34 to 75 years; a second tenant converts about 90% to 97% of its revenue to profit.; assumptions note: Gate thresholds are the practitioners' own: no build without a signed anchor, underwrite to two signed tenants, match land control to payback, and stress-test an anchor exit that cuts revenue 60% and profit about 78%.; note: Sources: Economic Oddities (QdFbgvbJJ-M @ 00:09:49, 00:08:28, 00:10:56); Holly Lane Radio (RRrHddpY1pU @ 00:24:22, 00:17:58); Mr. Finance (ku_-0C-ZnV4 @ 00:12:46); Profit Chain (t9bXdQI0jPM @ 00:08:38); Mr. Money (jQ79QHMZWQE @ 00:08:14).; chart type: decision_tree; nodes: gate: G1; question: Is a signed anchor tenant in hand before any steel goes up?; pass next: G2; fail action: Do not build; a single-tenant tower is a coin flip with a lease (Economic Oddities).; gate: G2; question: Does the price work on two signed tenants, not three hoped-for ones?; pass next: G3; fail action: Re-price; a price built on three future tenants is speculation dressed as infrastructure (Holly Lane Radio).; gate: G3; question: Does the ground-lease term cover the payback period?; pass next: G4; fail action: Extend land control first; an 11-year remaining ground lease under a producing tower is live exposure.; gate: G4; question: Does the deal survive an anchor exit and a carrier default?; pass next: Proceed to build or acquire; fail action: Pass; an anchor exit cuts revenue 60% and profit about 78%, and Crown's Dish claim exceeds $3.5B with recovery uncertain.

circle.title: gate: G1; question: Is a signed anchor tenant in hand before any steel goes up?; pass next: G2; fail action: Do not build; a single-tenant tower is a coin flip with a lease (Economic Oddities).

gate: G2; question: Does the price work on two signed tenants, not three hoped-for ones?; pass next: G3; fail action: Re-price; a price built on three future tenants is speculation dressed as infrastructure (Holly Lane Radio).

gate: G3; question: Does the ground-lease term cover the payback period?; pass next: G4; fail action: Extend land control first; an 11-year remaining ground lease under a producing tower is live exposure.

gate: G4; question: Does the deal survive an anchor exit and a carrier default?; pass next: Proceed to build or acquire; fail action: Pass; an anchor exit cuts revenue 60% and profit about 78%, and Crown's Dish claim exceeds $3.5B with recovery uncertain.

text.title: Assumptions: Gate thresholds are the practitioners' own: no build without a signed anchor, underwrite to two signed tenants, match land control to payback, and stress-test an anchor exit that cuts revenue 60% and profit about 78%.
